stem: Which punctuation mark belongs in the blank?
stimulus: Over one summer, a team of linguists documented an endangered language using three kinds of recordings: word lists, which covered kinship terms and numbers______ songs, which elders performed at harvest festivals; and everyday conversations, which were taped in family kitchens.
explanation: The sentence lists three recordings: word lists, songs and conversations. Each item has its own 'which' clause with commas inside it, and later in the sentence the songs and the conversations are separated by a semicolon. The blank separates the first item from the second, so it needs the same semicolon. This is the one check that decides SAT Boundaries questions about lists: before you choose, look at how the other items in the list are separated.

A.why: You looked only at the words beside the blank. A comma seems natural there, but the items already contain commas, so commas can no longer show where one item ends. The rest of the list uses a semicolon, and the blank must match it.

C.why: A colon introduces a list, and this list already has one after 'recordings.' A second colon in the middle of the list does not separate two items. It makes the sentence fall apart.

D.why: A period ends the sentence after the first item. That leaves 'songs, which elders performed...' as a fragment with no main verb, and it splits one list across two sentences.

stem: Which punctuation mark belongs in the blank?
stimulus: Textbooks often divide the immune system's white blood cells into three main groups: neutrophils, which are usually the first to reach an infection; B cells, which produce antibodies that tag invaders______ and T cells, which can destroy infected cells directly.
explanation: Look earlier in the sentence. The first item (neutrophils) is separated from the second (B cells) by a semicolon, because every item has a 'which' clause set off with a comma. The blank separates the second item from the third, so it takes a semicolon as well. You will use this skill on SAT Boundaries questions where the blank falls inside a long list: match the separator the list already uses.

A.why: A period ends the sentence before the last group is named. 'And T cells, which can destroy infected cells directly' cannot stand alone as a sentence, so this choice leaves a fragment.

B.why: The list is already introduced by the colon after 'groups.' A colon between the second and third items does not separate them. It breaks the sentence's structure.

C.why: This is the trap. Because 'B cells, which produce antibodies' already has a comma, another comma feels right. However, the earlier item boundary is a semicolon, and a comma here would make the B cells and T cells hard to tell apart from the commas inside them.

stem: Which punctuation mark belongs in the blank?
stimulus: During a week-long survey, divers counted three kinds of grazing animals on the reef: parrotfish, which scrape algae from dead coral; sea urchins, which feed mostly at night______ and surgeonfish, which travel in large, mixed schools across the shallows.
explanation: A semicolon after 'coral' separates the first and second items. Every item contains commas, including 'large, mixed' in the last one, so commas cannot do the job of separating items. The blank sits between the second and third items and needs the same semicolon. On SAT Boundaries questions with lists, check the other separators before you look at the choices.

B.why: You decided from the words around the blank. 'Sea urchins, which feed mostly at night,' looks as if it should close with a comma. But this list separates items with semicolons, and the blank has to match the one after 'coral.'

C.why: A period cuts the list in two. 'And surgeonfish, which travel in large, mixed schools across the shallows' has no main verb of its own, so it would be a fragment.

D.why: The colon after 'reef' has already introduced the list. A colon between two items does not separate them. It puts punctuation at a point where it makes no grammatical sense.

stem: Which punctuation mark belongs in the blank?
stimulus: In a survey of gig workers, economists asked about three sources of income insecurity: pay rates, which can change without notice; scheduling, which depends on fluctuating customer demand______ and benefits, such as health insurance, sick leave, and retirement plans, which most platforms do not provide.
explanation: The first two items, pay rates and scheduling, are separated by a semicolon. The third item has a whole list inside it (health insurance, sick leave, and retirement plans), full of commas. Semicolons are the only way to keep the three main items apart, so the blank takes a semicolon. This prepares you for the hardest list questions on the SAT, where one item contains a smaller list of its own.

A.why: This is the trap. The comma after 'scheduling' makes a closing comma at 'demand' look natural. But with commas this deep in the last item, a comma here would blur where one source of insecurity ends and the next begins. The list already uses a semicolon after 'notice,' so the blank must match it.

B.why: A period ends the sentence after two items. 'And benefits, such as health insurance... which most platforms do not provide' then stands alone without a main verb, so it is a fragment.

D.why: The colon after 'insecurity' has already done the job of introducing the list. Adding a colon between the second and third items breaks the list instead of separating its items.
